title: Sesame seeds: calcium, protein and fats

seo.title: Sesame seeds: calcium, protein, fats and serving size
seo.meta_description: Whole dried sesame provides 17.7 g protein, 49.7 g fat and 975 mg calcium per 100 g, but serving size and whether the hull remains change the story.
seo.search_intent: Understand sesame-seed nutrition, especially calcium, protein and fat

excerpt: Whole dried sesame is extremely concentrated: per 100 g it provides about 573 calories, 17.7 g protein, 49.7 g fat, 11.8 g fiber and 975 mg calcium. But 100 g is not a typical sprinkle. At 10 g, that becomes about 57 calories, 1.8 g protein and 98 mg calcium. The hull also matters greatly, so hulled seeds and tahini can contain far less calcium than the whole-seed reference.
content_html:
Sesame is usually eaten by the spoonful, scattered over bread, salads or sauces—not as a 100 g bowl. That makes serving size central to interpreting its nutrition. The seed is dense in fat, minerals and protein by weight, but most people eat a relatively small amount at once.

What whole sesame contains

The USDA reference for whole dried sesame provides per 100 g about 573 calories, 17.7 g protein, 49.7 g fat, 11.8 g fiber, 975 mg calcium, 351 mg magnesium and 14.6 mg iron.

At 10 g, those figures become roughly 57 calories, 1.8 g protein, 5.0 g fat, 1.2 g fiber, 98 mg calcium, 35 mg magnesium and 1.5 mg iron.

Most of the calories come from fat

Of the nearly 50 g fat per 100 g, most is unsaturated: about 18.8 g monounsaturated and 21.8 g polyunsaturated, compared with roughly 7 g saturated fat. The seed is therefore energy-dense even though its fat profile is predominantly unsaturated.

The calcium number needs an asterisk

The famous 975 mg/100 g figure belongs to whole sesame with its outer layer intact. It should not be assigned automatically to hulled sesame or every jar of tahini. A current USDA Foundation analysis of creamy sesame butter, for example, contains only about 116 mg calcium/100 g.

Hull removal and the particular raw material used can dramatically change the final number. If calcium is a major reason you buy sesame, product-specific nutrition data are more useful than a generic seed value.

Is sesame high in protein?

At 17.7 g/100 g, the concentration is substantial. But 10 g supplies only about 1.8 g protein and 30 g about 5.3 g. A sprinkle contributes protein; it rarely serves as the main protein source in a meal.

Iron and magnesium are concentrated too

Thirty grams of the whole-seed reference would provide roughly 4.4 mg iron and 105 mg magnesium. As with other seeds, measured mineral content is not the same as the amount absorbed: phytate and other compounds can reduce mineral bioavailability.

The useful takeaway has two parts: whole sesame is mineral-dense, and both the amount eaten and whether the hull remains can substantially change what reaches the plate.

faq.question: How much calcium is in sesame seeds?
faq.answer: The whole dried reference contains about 975 mg/100 g, but 10 g provides about 98 mg and hulled sesame or tahini may contain far less.

faq.question: How much protein is in a spoonful of sesame?
faq.answer: Using 10 g as a practical example, about 1.8 g protein.

faq.question: Are sesame seeds high in fat?
faq.answer: Yes. The whole dried reference contains about 49.7 g/100 g, mostly mono- and polyunsaturated fats.

faq.question: Does tahini contain as much calcium as whole sesame?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The USDA tahini reference used here contains about 116 mg/100 g, far below whole unhulled sesame.
